classification.difficultyReason: Compare three factor trees and explain why including 1 fails to give only prime factors.

content.prompt: Choose the correct factor tree for 21 and explain why the others are incorrect.

spec.description: A. The root 21 branches directly to 7 on the left and 3 on the right.
spec.answerVisibility: All option labels, numbers and branches are permanent student-visible givens; no correctness mark is supplied.

spec.description: B. The root 21 branches to 1 on the left and 21 on the right. The right-hand 21 branches to 3 on the left and 7 on the right.
spec.mathematics: 21 = 1 × 21 and 21 = 3 × 7, but the terminal factor 1 is not prime.
spec.answerVisibility: All option labels, numbers and branches are permanent student-visible givens; no correctness mark is supplied.

spec.description: C. The root 21 branches to the expression 3 × 1 on the left and 7 × 1 on the right.
spec.mathematics: The displayed product is (3 × 1)(7 × 1) = 21, but it includes 1, which is not a prime factor.
spec.answerVisibility: The multiplication expressions are permanent student-visible givens and must remain intact; no correctness mark is supplied.

answer.short: B and C are incorrect as 1 is not a prime number. Correct answer: A.
answer.worked: In A, $21=7\times3$, and both 7 and 3 are prime. B and C include 1, which is not prime, so they do not show a product consisting only of prime factors. Correct answer: A.
